criteria.connection_begin: Keep begin-time refusal and post-close begin under connection_failed with phase begin: codes name a connection event, the pool layer is where Can reports connection events, and transaction_failed is then never about merely reaching the server.
criteria.review_needed: The supplied facts do not discriminate, or each candidate violates something required.
criteria.transaction_begin: Keep begin-time refusal and post-close begin under transaction_failed with phase begin: open already vouched for the connection, entry is what just failed, and a single entry error simplifies every caller.

begin_failure_error.instructions: From common plus topics.begin_failure_error, pick the error for a native begin that is refused or meets a closed pool.

criteria.opaque_random: Prefer a per-attempt random identifier: unique by construction while exposing neither which pool ran nor how many attempts preceded it.
criteria.review_needed: Neither ID shape is separable on these facts, or both breach a requirement.
criteria.structured_sequence: Prefer an ID built from pool resource identity and a per-pool attempt counter: every report stays correlatable and tests can match it exactly, without embedding any driver payload.

commit_unknown_id.instructions: From common plus topics.commit_unknown_id, pick the contents of transaction_id on commit_unknown.

criteria.bounded_drain: Prefer a deadline on the drain: whatever has not settled in time converts to transaction_failed with phase drain and blocks the commit, so commit delay has a ceiling even against a stuck sublease.
criteria.review_needed: This evidence leaves the timing choice open, or disqualifies each policy.
criteria.unbounded_drain: Prefer waiting out the drain without limit: the pending native callback simply outlasts slow subleases, no timer kills legitimate work, and owner-scope drains already behave this way.

drain_bound.instructions: From common plus topics.drain_bound, pick bounded or unbounded waiting for the pre-commit drain.

fixed_constraints: Catalogue terms for sql::with_transaction<T>: errors connection_failed plus transaction_failed plus commit_unknown; phase strings on the leading two, a transaction_id string on the third. Callback signature sql::transaction into sql::decision<T> with zero emits; decision leaves are exactly the value-carrying records commit<T> and rollback<T>.

Bun 1.4.2 measurements: begin fulfills with the callback result on the commit path and rejects with the thrown identical on the abort path, which keeps a sentinel checkable by identity. Native begin refusal is PostgresError ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_REFUSED; begin after close is PostgresError ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_CLOSED. begin called on tx fails natively while recommending savepoints; statements issued after an in-transaction failure come back 25P02. tx and pool clients share one tagged-template call shape.

Scope discipline allows a single live transaction scope: nested with_transaction admission and stale or escaped handle dereference both throw invalid() and land as standard resource_state failures. Rollback travels as a private sentinel throw recognized beyond begin; commit is withheld until scope drain ends; the retained primary standard failure dominates secondary cleanup noise; post-commit-decision native rejection is commit_unknown, attempted exactly once.

Value encoding, row decoding and error classification for in-transaction queries are the I35 ones: classification is PostgresError-only, foreign throws keep to the generic fault path, and only sanitized fields may enter diagnostics, with message, detail, URL and credentials excluded.
common.purpose: Settle the Can transaction items purely from this request payload. Do not consult outside sources, do not build anything, do not narrate. If the payload ties the options, select the uncertainty marker.

begin_failure_error.facts: with_transaction already lists both errors, each phased. Native codes frame the begin failures as connection events, although they interrupt entry into a transaction on a pool whose open had succeeded. The begin phase label fits on either error.

commit_unknown_id.facts: commit_unknown has a lone transaction_id string that diagnostics must be able to print, ruling out driver payload and credential content. The runtime can either combine pool resource identity with an attempt tally or draw new randomness per attempt; the proxy-based uncertainty check accepts any present, safe value.

drain_bound.facts: The settled callback flips its scope to closing; owners then drain with the native begin callback held pending, and commit waits for drain completion. In-flight subleases run to completion. Supervisor-observed unsettled owners remain a required, visible test outcome under either timing rule.
